Snacking can make or break a diet. I used to keep them in my house for little bits of indulgence, but honestly I don't have that kind of self control once I'm 5 bowls deep. So! Healthy snacks to the rescue.

  • REAL cheese. No processed bullshit. Yes, it's more expensive - that's because it tastes better and thus more satisfying.

  • Olives. Very savory, a little goes a long way. Often paired with cheese.

  • Cured meats. Basically I'm talking about charcuterie at this point. Extra points if you bake some meat slices to extract the extra grease... Pat them down and you have meat chips. Fucking delicious.

  • Garbanzo beans. Baked till crispy. Oh, how I love thee like a summer's day... But seriously, you can make them any flavor and have serious umami.

  • Frozen bananas. Throw these in the blender with nothing else and you'll have ice cream in a few minutes. Add fruit, cocoa powder, tahini, honey... the combinations are endless. A large bowl (two bananas) is 250-300 calories after you add a bunch of stuff to it.
Olives are my go to snack. If I'm having a craving for something I know I shouldnt eat, 2 or 3 olives and bam, craving gone. I guess this works for others too!

I put 4 or 5 green olives and one oz. shredded sharp cheddar cheese in my salad. Really adds to the flavor. I only use 2 measured tablespoons of Caesar salad dressing so that it dosen't over flavor the olives and the other stuff in my salad. It blows my mind when people make a salad and then drench it with 1000 - 1500 calories of dressing... and then wonder why they don't lose weight.
Oh hell I never thought about meat chips. I Love my salted pork products. I'm making salami chips. Thank ya.

Man, do NOT keep dried fruits around as a snack. That shit is like my greatest weakness, I can put away raisins like a fat kid being told his mom is going to be putting up the Halloween candy. Or cranberries. Or those dehydrated fruit snacks. They're so fucking bad for you but theyre my favorite. Nuts too.

People think, especially people I know, that granola/dried fruits and that type of shit is "healthy". It's not! It's like my secret shame, I add an extra couple of miles to my bike ride when I eat it..
Well I'm not advocating that you gorge on them... A single serving is very satisfying

My diet is mostly eggs, chicken, white rice, beans, cottage cheese, whole milk, whole greek yogurt, russet potatoes broccoli and asparagus. I find that if I am eating clean, that I often have to force myself to eat to get enough protein and calories.

It's easier to exercise self-control once a week in the grocery store than every day in your refrigerator. Don's drink booze unless you can fit it into your macros. Don't be lazy, don't be gluttonous, show some self control.

Honestly, you can eat more or less whatever you want as long as you exhibit portion control. Controlling added fat and sugar intake is key. I overeat some days IF it's a worthwhile treat (a shitty Dunkin Donuts donut is NOT but a French pastry from a Michelin-starred patissier IS). I just eat a little less and work out a little harder the next day or two. It's honestly about moderation and making good choices MOST of the time.

I don't snack at all unless im really hungry (as opposed to wanting to eat something/having cravings, which hams cannot distinguish) . I eat 3 meals a day, usually something like yogurt and fruit for breakfast, a small sandwich for lunch and a couple eggs or some chicken with a side of veggies for dinner. The only refined carby food I eat on a regular basis is baguettes, we have a nice bakery by my apt so i go pick up a loaf every few days. I only take the width of my hand at a time. I normally drink water (preferably seltzer) unsweetened iced tea, diet soda and coffee or tea with 1 tsp of sugar and a splash of whole milk, no juice or beetusy shit. I like to go out to eat every or every other week depending on how broke I am, usually I get Thai or Chinese food

I'm not much of a breakfast person, but I usually force myself to have a frozen-fruit smoothie in the morning on the way to work. I try to keep it under 200 calories.

Lunch is typically a sandwich, often with turkey breast, but sometimes egg salad and tuna (if you've never tried a sandwich that's half egg salad and half tuna salad, I'd highly recommend it!) I'll usually pair the sandwich with a salad (little to no dressing) or fresh veggies.

Dinner varies, but is usually chicken or fish as a protein, with steamed veggies or a salad, and sometimes whole grain rice. I hardly ever eat red meat; maybe only a few times a month. I try to keep dinners under 600 calories.

Dessert is either yogurt or fruit. Sometimes I'll cheat and have an ice cream if I take my dog for a walk on the beach (there's a great ice cream parlor on the boardwalk!) and we usually end up splitting it :)

I don't generally keep things like chips, chocolate, cupcakes, etc. in the house. If I've got a bad craving (ie. that time of the month) I'll walk to the store and get what it is I'm craving at that specific moment.

I also portion out all my snacks for the week, generally on Sundays. I find it's easier to grab a pre-portioned pack of nuts, rather than eat them mindlessly from the bag and not know how much I'm eating
